title: Integral nonopposite Chevalley exponential commutator identity
statement:
Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional split semisimple Lie algebra over $\mathbf Q$ [def-wf-lie-algebra, def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra], with split Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, reduced crystallographic root system $R\subset\mathfrak h^\vee$ and Chevalley basis in the conventions of [lem-sfb-chevalley-admissible-representation]. Explicitly $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\gamma\in R}\mathbf Qe_\gamma$, the simple coroots form a basis of $\mathfrak h$, $[h,e_\gamma]=\gamma(h)e_\gamma$, $[e_\gamma,e_{-\gamma}]=h_\gamma$, and $[e_\gamma,e_\delta]=\pm(p_{\gamma,\delta}+1)e_{\gamma+\delta}$ when the sum is a root, where $p_{\gamma,\delta}=\max\{p\ge0:\delta-p\gamma\in R\}$; the bracket is zero if the sum is neither a root nor zero. Let $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbf Q}(W)$ be a representation on a finite-dimensional rational vector space. Let $\Lambda\subset W$ be a full lattice, meaning finite free over $\mathbf Z$ with $\Lambda\otimes\mathbf Q=W$, stable under $D_{\gamma,m}=\rho(e_\gamma)^m/m!$ for all $\gamma\in R$ and $m\ge0$, and assume each $\rho(e_\gamma)$ is nilpotent. For each commutative ring $A$ put $x_\gamma(a)=\sum_{m\ge0}(D_{\gamma,m}\otimes1)a^m\in\operatorname{End}_A(\Lambda\otimes A)$ for $a\in A$; the sum is finite. Fix $\alpha,\beta\in R$ with $\alpha\ne\beta$ and $\alpha\ne-\beta$. Order the finite set $S_{\alpha,\beta}=\{(i,j)\in\mathbf Z_{>0}^2:i\alpha+j\beta\in R\}$ by any total order refining nondecreasing $i+j$. There are integers $c_{\alpha,\beta;i,j}$, depending only on the chosen Chevalley basis and this order, such that for every $A$ and $u,v\in A$ one has
$$x_\alpha(u)x_\beta(v)x_\alpha(-u)x_\beta(-v)=\prod_{(i,j)\in S_{\alpha,\beta}}x_{i\alpha+j\beta}(c_{\alpha,\beta;i,j}u^iv^j).$$
This is a polynomial matrix identity over $\mathbf Z[u,v]$, not only an equality on field-valued points; no faithfulness, weight-lattice generation or reductivity hypothesis is needed. An empty product is the identity.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-string-central-parity] to $(\alpha,\beta)$, obtaining its ordering $(a,b)$, the independent roots $a,b$, and $q,Y_k,c_k,C_d,z_d$. Fix this choice in the rational Lie algebra, before choosing a representation. Write $B=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbf Q}(W)$, $H=\rho(e_a)$, and $\bar Y_k=\rho(Y_k)$. By [def-wf-lie-algebra], $\rho$ preserves brackets. Thus $\bar Y_k=c_k\rho(e_{b+ka})$ for $0\leq k\leq q$, and every $[\bar Y_i,\bar Y_j]$ commutes with every $\bar Y_k$. Their brackets also commute with each other: an element commuting with $X$ and $Y$ commutes with $XY-YX$, by expanding the products. Work in $B[[s,t]]$, with central variables; all formal exponentials below have arguments in $(s,t)B[[s,t]]$. Put $E_\gamma(w)=\exp(w\rho(e_\gamma))$.

proof.text:
Repeated expansion of $[H,-]$ gives
$$(\operatorname{ad}H)^n(V)=\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^j\binom nj H^{n-j}VH^j.$$
The induction step follows by subtracting the right multiplication by $H$ from the left multiplication and using Pascal's identity. Comparing coefficients of $s^n$ therefore gives
$$E_a(s)\rho(e_b)E_a(-s)=\sum_{k=0}^q s^k\bar Y_k.$$
Here the truncation is precisely $Y_k=0$ for $k>q$ in [lem-sfb-chevalley-string-central-parity]. Also $E_a(s)E_a(-s)=1$: its positive-degree coefficient is $H^n(1-1)^n/n!$. Conjugation by this inverse pair preserves every power of $\rho(e_b)$, so expansion in powers of $t$ yields
$$K_{ab}:=E_a(s)E_b(t)E_a(-s)E_b(-t)=\exp\!\left(t\sum_{k=0}^q s^k\bar Y_k\right)E_b(-t).$$
Each coefficient comparison uses finite sums, with no convergence assertion.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-formal-class-two-exponential] to the list
$$ts\bar Y_1,\ ts^2\bar Y_2,\ldots,ts^q\bar Y_q,\ t\bar Y_0.$$
All triple brackets vanish by [lem-sfb-chevalley-string-central-parity]. Reversing the positions of $Y_0,Y_k$ relative to the increasing list $Y_0,\ldots,Y_q$ changes its half-bracket sum by $-[Y_0,Y_k]$. With $Y_d=0$ for $d>q$, set
$$D_d=-C_d+[Y_0,Y_d]\quad(1\leq d\leq2q).$$
The correction argument is therefore $\sum_{d=1}^{2q}s^dt^2\rho(D_d)$. It commutes with every $\bar Y_k$, by Step 1. Move it past $E_b(-t)$; the adjacent $E_b(t)E_b(-t)$ cancel by the binomial calculation in Step 2. Thus
$$K_{ab}=\left(\prod_{k=1}^q E_{b+ka}(c_ks^kt)\right)\exp\!\left(\sum_{d=1}^{2q}s^dt^2\rho(D_d)\right).$$
The first product is in increasing $k$. The formula also applies when $q=0$, giving $K_{ab}=1$.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, printed pp.508--509, and equation (153), p.510; agent-written formal calculation from the cited root-string/parity and class-two identities. Appendix C, pp.621--622, explains the rank-two input.

proof.text:
Each $D_d$ is an integer multiple $w_de_{2b+da}$ if $2b+da\in R$, and is zero otherwise. Indeed $C_d=z_de_{2b+da}$ with $z_d\in\mathbf Z$ by [lem-sfb-chevalley-string-central-parity]; for $d\leq q$, $[Y_0,Y_d]=c_d[e_b,e_{b+da}]$ has an integer coefficient by the assumed Chevalley bracket formula, and for $d>q$ it is zero. Independence of $a,b$ excludes opposite roots in this bracket. The $D_d$ commute with all $Y_k$ and with each other, since they are linear combinations of their central brackets. Applying [lem-sfb-formal-class-two-exponential] to these commuting correction summands gives
$$K_{ab}=\left(\prod_{k=1}^q E_{b+ka}(c_ks^kt)\right)\left(\prod_{\substack{1\leq d\leq2q\\2b+da\in R}}E_{2b+da}(w_ds^dt^2)\right).$$
Every nonidentity factor is indexed by a pair of positive integers, and every coefficient was fixed in $\mathfrak g$ independently of $\rho$.

source.place: Section 23h, Theorem 23.71, printed pp.508--509, and equation (153), p.510; agent-written formal calculation from the cited root-string/parity and class-two identities. Appendix C, pp.621--622, explains the rank-two input.

proof.text:
Arrange these factors in the specified order on $S$. A correction factor commutes with every string factor, so moving it changes no coefficient. To reverse the order of two string factors with arguments $X=\varepsilon s^kt\bar Y_k$ and $Y=\varepsilon' s^lt\bar Y_l$ ($\varepsilon,\varepsilon'\in\{1,-1\}$), compare [lem-sfb-formal-class-two-exponential] for the lists $(X,Y)$ and $(Y,X)$. Since their bracket is central by [lem-sfb-chevalley-string-central-parity], it gives
$$\exp X\exp Y=\exp Y\exp X\exp([X,Y]).$$
The last bracket is $s^{k+l}t^2$ times the image of $\varepsilon\varepsilon'[Y_k,Y_l]$. Its Chevalley coefficient is an integer, and its root is $2b+(k+l)a$; if that is not a root the bracket is zero. Such new factors are central, so they can be collected immediately. Combining factors on the same root adds their parameters, by the binomial theorem. Adjacent inversion removal terminates, since it decreases the inversion count of the finite list of string factors; central insertions do not enter that count. If $(a,b)=(\alpha,\beta)$, use $s=u,t=v$. If $(a,b)=(\beta,\alpha)$, first use the group identity $K_{ba}=K_{ab}^{-1}$: invert the displayed product by reversing its factors and negating their arguments, then apply the same swaps and put $s=v,t=u$. This proves the required ordered formal identity in either orientation. Insert identity factors (coefficient zero) at all unused pairs of $S$. All swaps preserve root bidegrees, so parameters remain integer multiples of the required monomials $u^iv^j$.

proof.text: Choose a $\mathbf Z$-basis of the finite free lattice $\Lambda$. Every $D_{\gamma,m}$ has an integer matrix in this basis by lattice stability, and is zero for sufficiently large $m$ by the assumed nilpotence. Thus each $E_\gamma(cu^iv^j)$ occurring in Step 5 is a finite matrix polynomial over $\mathbf Z[u,v]$; the same holds for the four factors on the left. Their difference maps to zero in $\operatorname{Mat}_{\operatorname{rank}\Lambda}(\mathbf Q[[u,v]])$ by Step 5. The map $\mathbf Z[u,v]\to\mathbf Q[[u,v]]$ is injective: each integer coefficient maps to that identical rational coefficient, which can vanish only if the integer is zero. Hence the difference is zero already over $\mathbf Z[u,v]$. Applying the coefficient map $\mathbf Z[u,v]\to A$, $u\mapsto u$, $v\mapsto v$, proves the identity over every commutative ring $A$, including rings with torsion or nilpotents. Rank-zero lattices cause no exception, since there are no matrix entries to check. If $S$ is empty, every factor in Step 4 is absent, so the product is the identity. The construction of the integers used only the chosen root vectors, root-string choice and order, and required no faithfulness or group-theoretic hypothesis.
